turns.text: asked the Minister for National Development in the past three years, of the divorces filed where the couples co-own HDB flats, what is the proportion of (i) the matrimonial flats being sold on the open market and (ii) the divorcees being able to own flats after selling their matrimonial flats.

turns.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
turns.text: From 2021 to 2023, about half of co-owned flats that underwent transactions due to divorce were sold on the open market, while the other half was transferred to one of the divorced parties. A very small number of flats were surrendered to Housing and Development Board (HDB) as neither party was willing and able to retain the flat, and the flat was not eligible to be sold on the open market. In the same period, about 12,800 divorcees bought a resale flat or booked a new flat, either with their children or on their own. HDB does not track whether they had previously sold a matrimonial flat.

reports.report_type: Written Answers to Questions for Oral Answer Not Answered by End of Question Time
reports.title: New and Existing Worker Dormitories That Have Fulfilled Interim and New Standards for Better Living Conditions
reports.mp_names: Dr Tan See Leng,Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang

turns.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
turns.text: asked the Minister for Manpower what percentage of (i) new dormitories and (ii) existing dormitories have informed the Ministry of their plans to start work earlier to meet the interim standards and New Dormitory Standards, respectively, under the Dormitory Transition Scheme to improve living conditions for dormitory residents.

turns.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
turns.text: Today, about 200 dormitories, with a combined capacity of 70,000 beds, already meet the new dormitory standards. These include all new dormitories that were licensed after September 2021, which are required by law to meet the new dormitory standards. Of the remaining dormitories required to transition to interim standards by 2030, 14 have either commenced works or informed the Ministry of Manpower of their transition plans. The 14 dormitories have a combined capacity of about 100,000 beds, and account for about half the number of beds that need to meet the interim standards by 2030.

reports.title: Training Programmes Teachers Undergo to Teach High-ability Learners in Primary School and Their Effectiveness
reports.mp_names: Mr Chan Chun Sing,Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman

turns.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Bin Aliman
turns.text: asked the Minister for Education (a) whether the Ministry can provide more details on the specific training programmes that teachers undergo to teach high-ability learners in primary schools, including the duration and content of such training; (b) how will the Ministry ensure that these trained teachers are effectively identifying and nurturing high-ability learners across diverse educational contexts; and (c) what metrics or tools are used to assess the effectiveness of the teaching strategies employed by these teachers.

turns.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
turns.text: This question has been answered as part of Minister for Education’s oral reply on 10 September 2024 to Parliamentary Questions raised on the Gifted Education Programme. Member may refer to the transcript for the reply. [Please refer to "Outcomes from Gifted Education Programme, and Rationale and Plans for Programme Revamp", Official Report, 10 September 2024, Vol 95, Issue 141, Oral Answers to Questions section.]

reports.title: Attendance at Performances, Shows or Exhibitions of Arts Groups Other Than Own Ethnic Group
reports.mp_names: Ms Usha Chandradas,Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai

turns.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas
turns.text: asked the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (a) whether the Ministry tracks the number of Chinese audience members who attend the performances, shows or exhibitions of arts groups of ethnic minorities who conduct such activities (i) showcasing their respective minority cultures or (ii) in a language other than English or Mandarin; and (b) if so, what are the recent statistics.

turns.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas
turns.text: asked the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (a) whether the Ministry tracks the number of non-Chinese audience members who attend the performances, shows or exhibitions of Chinese arts groups who conduct such activities (i) showcasing Chinese culture; or (ii) in a language other than English; and (b) if so, what are the recent statistics.

turns.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
turns.text: The Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth does not collect data on the ethnicity of audience members who attend at each performance.

reports.report_type: Written Answers to Questions for Oral Answer Not Answered by End of Question Time
reports.title: Sustainability of Public Transport Services with Recent Fare Increases and Additional Government Subsidy
reports.mp_names: Mr Chee Hong Tat,Ms Poh Li San

turns.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
turns.text: asked the Minister for Transport with regard to the recent fare increase announced by the Public Transport Council (a) whether the public transport services remain economically sustainable moving forward, given that the Ministry provided an additional $250 million subsidy this year; and (b) how does Singapore fare in terms of transport fare increases compared to other large cities with similar public transport systems, such as Hong Kong, Seoul and Taipei, over the last four years.

turns.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
turns.text: I thank the Member for her question. We have received related questions for the subsequent Sitting. I will address them together in my reply at the 16 October 2024 Parliament Sitting. [Please refer to "Impact on Public Transport Operators' Viability and on Commuters when Recommended Fare Increases are Deferred", Official Report, 16 October 2024, Vol 95, Issue 144, Oral Answers to Questions section.]

reports.report_type: Written Answers to Questions for Oral Answer Not Answered by End of Question Time
reports.title: Safety Testing and Maintenance Requirements for Motorised Personal Mobility Aids Stored in HDB Flats
reports.mp_names: Miss Rachel Ong,Mr Chee Hong Tat

turns.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
turns.text: asked the Minister for Transport whether the Ministry will consider subjecting motorised Personal Mobility Aids (PMAs) that are stored in HDB flats to third-party safety testing and regular maintenance requirements to ensure safety of users and neighbours of surrounding HDB flats.

turns.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
turns.text: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) is studying the standards for lithium-ion batteries in personal mobility aids (PMAs), as part of regularly reviewing safety standards for PMAs, as well as other measures to enhance safety for both device users and the public. LTA and the Singapore Civil Defence Force will continue to educate the public on the safe usage of active mobility devices through campaigns, such as the "Be Device-Safe Programme". Active mobility device users are reminded to use only original batteries and maintain their devices according to manufacturer guidelines and not to modify their devices.

reports.report_type: Written Answers to Questions for Oral Answer Not Answered by End of Question Time
reports.title: Allocated Spaces and Time-controlled Charging Points in HDB Car Parks for Motorised Personal Mobility Aids
reports.mp_names: Miss Rachel Ong,Mr Chee Hong Tat

turns.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
turns.text: asked the Minister for Transport whether there can be allocated spaces and time-controlled charging points in HDB carparks for motorised personal mobility aids, with priority charging given to those staying in smaller HDB flats with space limitations.

turns.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
turns.text: Currently, motorised personal mobility aids and other motorised active mobility devices (AMDs), such as power-assisted bicycles and motorised personal mobility devices, do not require special charging infrastructure and can be charged using standard wall sockets found at home. We urge AMD users to practise safe charging practices, such as maintaining their devices based on the manufacturer’s guidelines and not to modify their devices. I thank the Member for her suggestion of having public charging points in Housing and Development Board carparks. We will assess if this could help to enhance safety for device users and the public.

reports.report_type: Written Answers to Questions for Oral Answer Not Answered by End of Question Time
reports.title: Prohibiting Smoking in Area Directly under MRT or LRT Viaducts
reports.mp_names: Mr Gan Thiam Poh,Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien

turns.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
turns.text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment whether the Ministry will consider prohibiting smoking in the area directly under MRT or LRT viaducts.

turns.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
turns.text: The National Environment Agency (NEA) adopts a pragmatic approach in identifying places where smoking should be prohibited and takes into consideration whether the places have high footfall, are frequented by families, or are air-conditioned or enclosed. To reduce the public’s exposure to the harmful effects of second-hand tobacco smoke, NEA has progressively extended the smoking prohibition to cover more than 49,000 places island-wide. This includes covered and underground pedestrian walkways, playgrounds and void decks. There are currently no plans to specifically prohibit smoking in areas under Mass Rapid Transit and Land Transport Authority viaducts. We encourage smokers to exercise social responsibility and be considerate when smoking in public spaces.

reports.report_type: Written Answers to Questions for Oral Answer Not Answered by End of Question Time
reports.title: Translation Tools in School Apps to Support Parents and Caregivers Whose First Language is Not English
reports.mp_names: Mr Chan Chun Sing,Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan

turns.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
turns.text: asked the Minister for Education whether the Ministry will consider offering a translation tool for digital resources, such as Parent Kits and Parents Gateway, to support parents and caregivers whose first language is not English.

turns.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
turns.text: Currently, parents and guardians can make use of in-device translation functions on smart devices to select and translate relevant parts of any digital text, or scan images of text for translation using free translation apps. These tools can be applied to Parents Gateway messages, Parent Kits and other education resources. Parents and guardians who need support can reach out to school staff. The Ministry of Education will continue to study ways to enhance our digital resources so that translations can be even more convenient for parents and guardians.

reports.report_type: Written Answers to Questions for Oral Answer Not Answered by End of Question Time
reports.title: Studies on Quantifiable Effects of Dense Urban Living Environment on Individuals’ Physiological Stress Responses
reports.mp_names: Ms He Ting Ru,Mr Desmond Lee

turns.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
turns.text: asked the Minister for National Development whether the Government has conducted any recent or ongoing studies to measure any quantifiable effects of a dense urban living environment on individuals’ physiological stress responses and, if so, to share the findings of these studies.

turns.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
turns.text: The Urban Redevelopment Authority, the Housing and Development Board and the Agency for Science, Technology and Research (A*STAR) Institute of Human Development and Potential have recently embarked on a three-year study on the impact of the urban environment on mental well-being, which will inform the way that we plan for a healthy living environment in Singapore. This study will build on current research, such as the benefits of greenery on mental well-being. We will share the findings when ready.

reports.title: Schedule for Completion of Active Ageing Centres from Proposed Increase in Budget
reports.mp_names: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim,Mr Ong Ye Kung

turns.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
turns.text: asked the Minister for Health what is the schedule, by region and on a quarterly basis, for the anticipated completion of Active Ageing Centres that will be funded by the proposed increase in budget for this purpose.

turns.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
turns.text: Since the inception of Active Ageing Centres (AACs) in 2021, the Ministry of Health and the Agency for Integrated Care have set up 208 AACs1. We will continue to scale this to 220 AACs by 2025. The AACs will be distributed across all parts of Singapore, such that eight in 10 seniors will have access to AAC activities near their homes by 2025. The locations of AACs, when confirmed, can be found on the SupportGoWhere website.

reports.title: Road Traffic Accidents and Fatality Rates in Past Five Years
reports.mp_names: Mr K Shanmugam,Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong

turns.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
turns.text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs in the past five years, what is the annual number of (i) road traffic accidents and (ii) road deaths per billion vehicle kilometres.

turns.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
turns.text: The Member may refer to the report on the Annual Road Traffic Situation 2023 on the Police’s website for the annual number of road traffic accidents. The Traffic Police (TP) do not track the number of road deaths per billion vehicle kilometres. TP tracks the number of road deaths per 100,000 population, which is one of the Global Health Observatory indicators, and Sustainable Development Goals tracked by the World Health Organization. TP also tracks the number of road deaths per 10,000 vehicles.

reports.title: Extension of Multi-Generation Priority Scheme to Include Single Unmarried Children in Joint Applications for BTO Flats
reports.mp_names: Mr Desmond Lee,Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim

turns.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
turns.text: asked the Minister for National Development whether the Multi-Generation Priority Scheme can be extended to include single unmarried children of elderly parents so that single children and their elderly parents can make joint applications for HDB flats in a BTO project and live proximate to one another.

turns.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
turns.text: Today, married children and their parents buying new flats to live with or near one another, get priority access to Build-To-Order flats. As announced at the National Day Rally in August 2024, from mid-2025 onwards, we will extend such priority access to all parents and their children, married and single. The Ministry of National Development will share more details when ready.

reports.title: Current Percentage and Future Plans for All Cycling Lanes to Be Grade-separated from Footpaths
reports.mp_names: Mr Chee Hong Tat,Ms Hazel Poa

turns.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
turns.text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) what percentage of cycling lanes that run parallel to footpaths are currently fully grade-separated; (b) whether there are plans for all cycling lanes to be grade-separated from footpaths; and (c) if not, why not.

turns.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
turns.text: The Land Transport Authority and National Parks Board generally do not design grade-separated cycling paths that are adjacent to footpaths, and have no plans to do so moving forward. A grade-separated path, such as a raised cycling path, can be a tripping hazard for path users and make it difficult for wheelchair and personal mobility aid users to navigate the level differences between cycling paths and footpaths.

reports.title: Extension of Maternity Protection to Singaporeans Engaged in Non-standard Forms of Employment
reports.mp_names: Ms See Jinli Jean,Dr Tan See Leng

turns.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean
turns.text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) whether the Ministry will extend maternity protection to Singaporeans engaged in non-standard forms of employment, such as those under dependent self-employment to provide some recourse for termination of contracts on grounds related to pregnancy; and (b) if not, when will the Ministry consider doing so.

turns.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
turns.text: Self-employed persons and service buyers are encouraged to negotiate contracts that are mutually favourable, including providing for scenarios where a party is unable to fulfil the contract, such as pregnancy. Parties can take reference from the Tripartite Standard on Contracting with Self-Employed Persons, and any disputes can be brought to the Small Claims Tribunals.

reports.title: Death of Full-time National Serviceman at Pasir Laba Camp on 27 September 2024
reports.mp_names: Dr Ng Eng Hen,Mr Leong Mun Wai

turns.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
turns.text: asked the Minister for Defence whether he can provide further details concerning the death of a full-time National Serviceman at Pasir Laba Camp on 27 September 2024.

turns.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
turns.text: We refer the Member to the statement released by the Ministry of Defence (MINDEF) on 27 September 2024. As the Police investigation is ongoing and to respect the privacy of the late Serviceman’s family, it would not be appropriate for MINDEF and the Singapore Armed Forces (SAF) to divulge further details at this juncture. MINDEF and the SAF extend our deepest condolences to the family. We are extending to them our assistance during this time of grief.

reports.title: Number of Licence Applications Rejected under Debt Collection Act
reports.mp_names: Mr K Shanmugam,Ms Hany Soh

turns.speaker: Ms Hany Soh
turns.text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) whether any applications for a licence under the Debt Collection Act 2022 (DCA) have been rejected since the commencement of the DCA on 1 December 2023; and (b) if so, how many applications have been rejected and what are the reasons.

turns.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
turns.text: As of 30 September 2024, the Police have rejected six applications for a licence to operate a debt collection business under the Debt Collection Act. Police assessed that the applicants and key appointment holders do not fulfil the fit and proper criteria, including because of criminal antecedents of unlicensed moneylending and voluntarily causing hurt to others.

reports.title: Government’s Expectations for Population Growth over Next Five Years
reports.mp_names: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis,Ms Indranee Rajah

turns.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
turns.text: asked the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance whether the 2% year-on-year overall increase in Singapore’s total population as of June 2024 is in line with the Government’s expectations of population growth rates in the next five years.

turns.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah (for the Prime Minister)
turns.text: While Singapore’s total population increased by 2% from June 2023 to June 2024, the annualised growth rate over the last five years (2019-2024) has been lower, at 1.1%. This is in line with our expectation for our total population to remain significantly below 6.9 million by 2030, as stated at the Committee of Supply this year.

reports.title: Timelines for Establishment of Singapore College of Islamic Studies and First Intake of Students
reports.mp_names: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi,Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M

turns.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
turns.text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (a) what is the anticipated timeline for the formal establishment of the Singapore College of Islamic Studies; and (b) when will it be fully operational for the intake of its inaugural batch of students.

turns.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
turns.text: The Singapore College of Islamic Studies aims to develop our future Islamic religious teachers and scholars to provide sound and relevant religious guidance to Muslims in Singapore, in line with our multiracial and multi-religious context. More details about the college will be shared in due course.

reports.report_type: Written Answers to Questions for Oral Answer Not Answered by End of Question Time
reports.title: Pricing Guidelines for Plastic Bag Charge Imposed by Merchants
reports.mp_names: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim,Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien

turns.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
turns.text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment whether there are any plans to introduce pricing guidelines for amounts that merchants may levy for the plastic bag charge.

turns.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
turns.text: Supermarket operators with an annual turnover of more than $100 million are required to charge a minimum of five cents per disposable carrier bag, regardless of material and size, provided at their supermarket outlets. For all other retailers, charging for disposable carrier bags is a business decision. There are currently no plans for the Government to introduce pricing guidelines for these retailers.

reports.title: Restricting Numbers in Group Gatherings at HDB Common Areas during Quiet Hours
reports.mp_names: Mr Gan Thiam Poh,Mr K Shanmugam

turns.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
turns.text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs whether the Police will consider restricting the number of people gathering in groups and causing congregational noise at HDB common greens during the quiet hours after 10.30 pm and before 7.00 am.

turns.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
turns.text: The law sets out the circumstances when public gatherings require permit. In addition, the Police also take action when there are law and order issues. Where there are no law and order issues or where the gatherings do not require permit, the Police will generally not intervene or restrict such gatherings.

reports.title: Annual Hiring Targets for Healthcare Workers to Meet Projected Size of 82,000 by 2030
reports.mp_names: Mr Ong Ye Kung,Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang

turns.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
turns.text: asked the Minister for Health for each year over the next five years, what are the hiring targets for (i) nurses (ii) allied health professionals and (iii) support care staff, in order to meet the healthcare workforce size of 82,000 by 2030.

turns.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
turns.text: As our population ages, we can expect demand for healthcare services and manpower to increase. To attain a healthcare workforce size of 82,000 nationally by 2030, the Ministry of Health will need to recruit about 6,000 nurses, Allied Health Professionals and support care staff annually.

reports.title: Provision of Complimentary Tap Water for Paying Customers at Food and Beverage Establishments
reports.mp_names: Mr Ong Hua Han,Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien

turns.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han
turns.text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment whether the Ministry will consider mandating food and beverage establishments to provide tap water free of charge for paying customers to reduce plastic waste from bottled water.

turns.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
turns.text: There are currently no plans to mandate food and beverage (F&B) establishments to provide tap water free of charge for paying customers. Nonetheless, we encourage both F&B establishments and patrons to play a part in tackling plastic waste by reducing the excessive use of disposables.

reports.title: Importation of Nuclear-generated Energy
reports.mp_names: Mr Gan Kim Yong,Mr Gan Thiam Poh

turns.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
turns.text: asked the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry whether the Government will consider importing electricity or energy that is generated by nuclear plants from other countries.

turns.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
turns.text: Based on our current understanding, countries in the region are still studying the potential deployment of nuclear energy and have yet to make a firm decision on it. It is, therefore, premature to discuss importing electricity that is generated by nuclear plants from other countries.
